[0] At WWDC 2021, Apple announced support for storing IDs in Apple Wallet on iPhone. At the time, Apple described the feature as the final step toward letting you "completely ditch your physical wallet."

[1] Here are the states next in line to support Apple Wallet ID…

[2] Apple Wallet ID support

[3] Since Apple announced the feature five years ago, support has gradually expanded across the United States. Currently, iPhone and Apple Watch users in 14 states and Puerto Rico can add their ID or state ID to Apple Wallet. You can see the full list here:

[4] Where is the feature launching next? Here is everything we know so far.

[5] The following seven states have confirmed they are working on Apple Wallet ID support, have been listed as partners by Apple, or have appeared in Apple’s code:

  • [6] Kentucky (launching in “summer” 2026)
  • [7] North Carolina (launching in early 2027)
  • [8] Oklahoma (in development, launch date unknown)
  • [9] Utah (in development, launch date unknown)
  • [10] Virginia (in development, launch date unknown)
  • [11] Connecticut (status unknown, previously listed by Apple as a partner)
  • [12] Mississippi (status unknown, previously listed by Apple as a partner)

[13] Meanwhile, the Secure Technology Alliance has been tracking the rollout of mobile IDs across the United States. Here are some states that have begun exploring mobile ID support through legislation or research, but have not been mentioned by Apple:

  • [14] Indiana
  • [15] Vermont
  • [16] New Jersey
  • [17] Florida
  • [18] South Carolina
  • [19] Tennessee
  • [20] Missouri
  • [21] Nevada
  • [22] Wyoming

[23] It’s worth keeping in mind that progress varies significantly from state to state. A state exploring or developing digital ID support does not necessarily mean it will ultimately launch, let alone make its way to Apple Wallet.

[24] Wrap-up

[25] As you can see, the rollout of Apple Wallet ID across the United States remains quite scattered.

[26] However, you don’t have to wait for your state to support digital IDs in Apple Wallet before trying out the feature.

[27] Last year, Apple launched a new “digital ID” feature powered by your US passport. Although it isn’t your ID, you can use it at TSA checkpoints in over 250 airports across the United States with your iPhone.

[28] Have you stored your ID or driver’s license in Apple Wallet on your iPhone? Do you actually use it? Let us know in the comments.
